item.content:encoded:
Eh, I always though he was Adam gone bad, like Abel. I think there was something about Cain and Abel meeting him and now not being allowed near him again. Though I suppose it could sorta go both ways.

Except no way is the girl God. For one thing, Jesus knew who he was the whole time, so another incarnation would do the same. And Heaven wouldn't be empty if another incarnation happened. It wasn't empty when Jesus came; the Father and the Holy Spirit part of Him stayed up there (for a certain value of 'up there', since God is supposed to be everywhere, at least in essence).

If Clef was the devil, the whole anti-reality-warper thing could be just him being frustrated at not being able to beat God, so he beats the next-best thing. Still prefer the idea of him being Adam.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The incident preceding this interview captivated me, and this interview sealed it - nothing on this site will ever strike a chord with me like this Tale (though SCP-342 came close-ish). I'm sorry 239 got put in a coma…and she's God? Awesome! I love that God is a girl! One problem, though: If she is God, shouldn't she be taken out of the coma? I mean, God wouldn't manifest without some sort of purpose, and considering how 239 came to be in the custody of the Foundation, I'm thinking that that purpose probably has something to do with the Foundation. I mean, I also realize that Dr. Clef is a liar, but there's a small chance that it's the truth, and even if that chance is small, it's not really worth taking a risk, is it? Also, I would rather 239 be God incarnate than 343 - I like 239 a lot better.
Even more awesome, Dr. Clef is the Devil incarnate! Oh, how I wish he was real! I wish, so much, that I could talk to him! That, above all else, is why I love this site and the world of the Foundation, and why I always will, no matter what horrible things I find on this site or what outrageous injustices I read about the Foundation committing (i.e. putting 239 in a coma; she's a child, for crying out loud - it's not fair to do that to her!). Anyway, shine on, Lucifer!
